The readings differ only in the presence or absence of spaces and periods around the chapter and verse numbers (e.g., '31/ v.10.' vs '31. v.10.'), which are punctuation/formatting variations.
The readings differ only in the presence or absence of a period after 'cap. 31' and 'v. 10'.
The difference is the final 'e' (weis vs weiſe), which corresponds to a case or number ending (e.g., dative singular vs nominative/accusative, or plural vs singular) in early modern German.
Difference between long s (ſ) and short s (f) is a graphic variant.
The variants differ by the presence or absence of the letter 's' (erfrewet vs erfreuet vs erſreuet), which is a spelling variation of the same word form.
The readings differ in the word itself: '5' (numeral) vs 'Jhr' (abbreviation for Jahr/year). This is a difference in wording/lexeme, not just graphic form.
Difference in long s (ſ/s) and superscript e (ẽ) vs explicit e, same word form.
